section_summary: This section contains correspondence, military permits, entry applications, and policy circulars concerning travel to and exit from occupied Japan between January and March 1949. Major topics include GHQ SCAP Circular No. 1 governing private commercial entrants, proposals to liberalize tourist visits by overseas relatives of Japanese residents, and procedures for processing commercial travelers through the Pacific Military Permit Branch and foreign diplomatic missions. Individual cases involve business representatives, displaced persons, and foreign nationals seeking exit permits or transit clearance, including travelers from Burma, Iran, Brazil, China, and Peru.

subfiles.about: Comprehensive regulations governing entry, legal status, logistics, and conduct of private commercial entrants in Japan.
subfiles.from: GHQ SCAP (Mueller / Levy)
subfiles.summary: Comprehensive directive superseding previous circulars governing private commercial entrants to Japan. Establishes allowable entry purposes, application and sponsorship procedures, 60-day limits, customs, health registration, and legal jurisdiction under military and Japanese courts. Outlines logistical support including Boeki Cho commercial hotels, currency controls, and Eighth Army administrative responsibilities.
subfiles.title: GHQ SCAP Circular No. 1: Private Commercial Entrants
